mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and an increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a month-over-month decline in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in an economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: regime: late-cycle expansion AND RSAFS MoM < -0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when the regime is late-cycle expansion and RSAFS MoM < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE rises by at least 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals a weakening manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market reacts to deteriorating economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO MoM < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery, a month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.0% signals a strengthening housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates higher consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: regime: housing market recovery AND HOUST MoM > 1.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when the regime is housing market recovery and HOUST MoM > 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO declines and GDPC1 declines.
